chunks: Proceed, for there is no fear upon you, if Allah so wills.
So they proceeded safely, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ: If Allah wills; expressing dependence on the divine will
key_terms.اِمْضُوا: Go forward; continue on your way
key_terms.رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: Lord of all the worlds and creation

ai.seo_question: How does this narration show reliance upon Allah during fear and uncertainty?
ai.summary: This report conveys reassurance and trust in Allah through the instruction to proceed without fear, conditioned by divine will. It concludes by affirming the safe outcome and offering praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah Bin Salih, from his father, from Abu Ali Al Mutahhir, 
‘He wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) in the year of Al-Qadisiyya to let him<sup>asws</sup> know of the leaving (not performing Hajj) of the people and that he feared the thirst (due to the drought). So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Continue, and there would be no fear upon you, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
So Suleyman continued (to Hajj), and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from abu ‘Abdallah ibn Salih from his father from abu Ali al-Mutahhar the following. “He wrote to him (abu Muhammad (a.s.) in the year of Qadisiyya, the year of draught that forced people to returned home without performing Hajj for fear of thirst. He wrote back in reply, “continue your journey and you will have no fear by the will of Allah.”
They continued their journey to Hajj safely and thanks to Allah.”
